newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez aims to keep at least 50 pct of Tractabel.
newsitem.headline: Suez aims to keep at least 50 pct of Tractabel.

text.p: French financial holding company Cie de Suez, slated for a merger with utility giant Lyonnaise des Eaux, said on Wednesday it aimed to keep at least 50 percent of Tractebel.
The company denied a report in Belgian newspaper Financieel Economische Tijd that it had given written approval to a merger between Belgium's Tractebel and Electrabel.
"(Suez) recalls that energy (generation) is one of the four core activities of the group which will be formed after the merger of Suez-Lyonnaise des Eaux," it said in a statement.
"In this context, Suez, through its Societe Generale de Belgique SGB, intends to maintain a participation of at least 50 percent in Tractebel," it added.
Earlier on Wednesday, the Belgian government said it was in favour of a merger of Belgian utility holding company Tractebel SA with its unit Electrabel.
Electrabel, which has the largest capitalisation on the Brussels bourse, has a virtual monopoly on electricity production in Belgium.

A spokeswoman for Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said he had spoken with Suez head Gerard Mestrallet and SGB head Etienne Davignon, where he had suggested the merger. She added the two businessmen had voiced no objection.
The Financieel-Economische Tijd said Mestrallet had approved the merger idea in writing.
A joining-up of the two Belgian units would dispel fears over the impact of the planned merger between Suez and Lyonnaise on Tractebel, the paper said.
The Belgian government has repeatedly expressed fears that following the merger, Tractebel's foreign expansion would become subordinate to the French group's ambitions.
To counter such worries, Tractebel plans a change in its bylaws later this month, to turn the group into a so-called autonomous company with independent directors.
The merged group will have 42 percent of Electrabel.
The paper said a Tractebel-Electrabel merger would further dilute SGB's Tractebel stake to around 25 percent.
